sections.summary: Negative keywords are keywords used to exclude searches from triggering ads on Google Ads Search.

claims.text: Negative keywords let advertisers exclude searches from triggering their ads.
A negative keyword is written by adding a minus sign (-) in front of the keyword.

evidence.locator: Negative keywords: Add a minus sign - in front of your keyword to exclude searches.

sections.summary: The packet only states the minus-sign syntax and the exclusion effect; broader matching mechanics are not covered.

claims.text: Adding a minus sign in front of a keyword causes searches containing it to not trigger the ad.

sections.summary: No use case is stated in the evidence; the only editorial inference is avoiding unwanted search queries.

claims.text: Advertisers plausibly use negative keywords to stop irrelevant searches from triggering ads, reducing wasted impressions/clicks.
conditions: Editorial reasoning from the documented exclusion effect; no source states a use case or quantified savings.

sections.summary: The packet documents only the syntax (a minus sign before the keyword), not any menu path or step-by-step procedure.

claims.text: The documented setup element is the syntax: place a minus sign (-) in front of the keyword to be excluded.

evidence.locator: Negative keywords: Add a minus sign - in front of your keyword to exclude searches.

claims.text: The evidence does not document which menus, screens, or steps are used to add negative keywords.

sections.summary: The evidence says nothing about metrics, reporting, or performance effects of negative keywords.
The packet provides no cross-platform or cross-feature comparisons, so no relationship can be stated.
One official Google support source is provided; the packet carries no check date.

claims.text: Official source: Google Ads support, campaign creation guidance (source_id google.search.campaigns.create).
